title: POC Accelerator — Technical Chronicle and Integration Runbook
body:
Purpose and scope:
- Lightweight chronicle for a customer-facing POC: capture configuration steps, integration checkpoints, benchmark schedule, failure modes, and actionable owner tasks. Intended to be used during the technical workshop and the subsequent 3-week lab phase.

Summary of the engagement:
- Customer: FinReg Analytics (demo/early adopter).
- Primary use case: regulatory document summarization + semantic search over internal policy corpus (10k documents).
- Objective: validate quality (ROUGE/semantic recall), latency (p99 < 350ms for 512-token context on dedicated instance), and cost envelope (< $0.15 per 1k tokens at target throughput).
- Deliverables: workshop lab notebook, integration runbook, benchmark report, go/no-go acceptance checklist, and a sample fallback policy for degraded capacity.

Workshop agenda (Day 0 / Kickoff):
- 09:00 — 09:30: Intro + objectives (SE lead, customer eng, product manager).
- 09:30 — 10:15: Environment mapping (network, data stores, auth). Capture hostnames, VPC requirements, and KMS details.
- 10:15 — 11:00: Data ingestion plan + sample document walkthrough. Agree on 2 canonical doc sets (policy-100 / policy-1k subset).
- 11:00 — 12:30: Quickstart: spin up Redwood Dedicated sandbox (small GPU pool), deploy model variant (redwood-llama2-q4_7b) with quantization profile.
- 13:30 — 15:00: Integration checkpoints: API routes, streaming, embeddings pipeline, and retriever wiring.
- 15:00 — 16:00: Benchmark baseline run and metrics capture.
- 16:00 — 16:45: Risk review and mitigations.
- 16:45 — 17:00: Action items and owner assignments.

Pre-work / prerequisites (SE checklist):
- Customer provides sample dataset (S3 path or secure FTP) and an example of expected outputs (3 gold summaries).
- Security contact confirmed and IP allowlist for dedicated pool provided.
- KMS/HSM key alias available if customer requires encrypted model keys.
- GitHub repo forked: poc-samples (branch: finreg-poc).
- Create initial Redwood API key with restricted scope for lab use.

Environment configuration (record exact commands used):
- Dedicated pool: rwdctl create-pool --name finreg-poc --gpu-type a10g --min 1 --max 2 --network vpc-analytics-east-1
- Model deploy: rwdctl deploy-model --pool finreg-poc --model redwood-llama2-q4_7b --quantization q4_0 --kvcache-enabled true --min-batch 4
- Embedding worker (K8s job): kubectl apply -f embedding-worker-finreg.yaml (use node selector: workload=embedding)
- Retriever: ElasticSearch v8 index 'finreg_policies_v1' with mapping version 2024-11-01

Integration checkpoints and verification steps:
1) Auth & Connectivity (owner: Diego) — verify API calls from customer VPC to Redwood Private endpoint using curl and curl --http2 for streaming. Log sample call and response.
2) Data pipeline (owner: Lina) — run ingestion for 100 docs and confirm embedding vector size matches model embedding dims. Capture failed items and root cause.
3) Retriever accuracy (owner: Markus) — run 20 query/recall tests, capture top-3 recall and MRR. Expected top-3 recall > 0.85 for gold queries.
4) Latency profile (owner: Priya) — run 1k sequential generation calls and 1k concurrent calls at target concurrency, collect p50/p90/p99.
5) Cost telemetry (owner: Aisha) — enable token accounting, validate cost-per-1k token estimate from the console match offline calculations.

Benchmark schedule and metrics to capture:
- Baseline runs: Day 0 after deploy (small dataset) — measure cold-start RTT, first-token latency, and throughput at batch sizes 1,4,8.
- Load runs: Day 3 — ramp to target QPS in 4 steps (10%, 40%, 70%, 100%) holding for 10 minutes each.
- Regression tests: Day 5 — synthetic prompt set (100 prompts), compute ROUGE-L and embedding cosine recall.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p99 generation latency, tokens/sec per GPU, cost per 1k tokens, top-3 retrieval recall, MRR, failure rate (HTTP 5xx).

Acceptance criteria (go/no-go):
- Functional: All integration checkpoints pass and retriever recall >= 0.85.
- Performance: p99 <= 350ms for typical 512-token context at 80% target load OR documented fallback that keeps p99 <= 600ms.
- Cost: projected unit cost <= $0.15 per 1k tokens at steady-state or documented optimization plan to achieve it within 2 weeks.
- Security & compliance: Data-in-transit encrypted, KMS integration validated, and shared access logs in customer S3.

Common failure modes & immediate mitigations (runbook snippets):
- Error: Model warmup high memory — mitigation: reduce min-batch to 1 and increase pool min to 2 nodes temporarily; capture heap profile and file a bug with infra team.
- Error: Retriever low recall — mitigation: check tokenizer differences, reindex with full-text + bigrams, bump embedding dim or switch model-embedding variant.
- Error: High 5xx rate under load — mitigation: enable circuit breaker route to fallback smaller model variant (redwood-llama2-q3_4b) and alert SRE.

Owner task tracker (week-by-week):
- Week 0 (Aisha): confirm customer infra, create repo branch, pre-seed sample S3, create initial infra PR (due: 2025-01-20).
- Week 1 (Diego): finish network tests, provisioning, and pool creation; deliver connectivity report (due: 2025-01-24).
- Week 1 (Lina): ingest first 1k docs and validate embeddings; report ingestion errors (due: 2025-01-27).
- Week 2 (Markus): run retrieval baseline, tune vector store, and produce recall table (due: 2025-02-03).
- Week 2 (Priya): run load/latency tests and collect telemetry, produce latency-cost curve (due: 2025-02-06).
- Week 3 (Aisha/SE): synthesize report and present go/no-go to customer (target: 2025-02-10).

Notes to self (informal / workshop scribbles):
- Customer nervous about PII leakage; recommend a data minimization step and redact titles in ingestion.
- Try prefix-caching for common policy intros to shave 30-60ms off p99 on repeat queries.
- Consider an early canary routing to hosted API if Dedicated pool is saturated during demo hours.

Deliverable checklist before handoff:
- [ ] Lab notebook with raw benchmark logs (s3://finreg-poc-logs/2025-01)
- [ ] Integration runbook (this doc + commands and scripts zipped)
- [ ] Acceptance checklist signed by customer PM and SE lead
- [ ] Post-POC optimization plan with 3 options (quantization-, batching-, or retriever-focused)
- [ ] Clean-up script for tearing down the dedicated pool and removing ephemeral keys

Follow-ups and open questions:
- Customer asks to evaluate a different model family for hallucination tests — need to schedule a model-swap run and update cost projection. (owner: Aisha)
- Confirm SLAs for dedicated demo pool during business hours; can we extend maintenance blackout window? (owner: Diego)
- Confluence doc to link full dataset schema and PII fields (linked_artifacts updated once available).

Appendix: quick command snippets and notes used in the lab (copyable)
- curl example (streaming):
  curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $RWD_KEY" "https://private.redwood.test/v1/generate?model=redwood-llama2-q4_7b" -d '{"prompt": "Summarize policy X in 3 bullets"}'

- sample ingestion flag (embedding-worker-finreg.yaml):
  env:
    - name: S3_PATH
      value: s3://finreg-samples/policy-subset-100
    - name: EMBEDDING_MODEL
      value: redwood-embed-v2

End of chronicle.

Revision log:
- 2025-01-15 Aisha: created initial chronicle and workshop agenda.
- 2025-01-24 Diego: added connectivity test notes and adjusted pool sizes after initial run.
- 2025-02-10 Aisha: updated acceptance criteria and added cost constraints per PM feedback.
